A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hier-COS/HOPS work by the same authors. Their main text and embedded appendices are readable, allowing methods, experiments, equations, and displays to be matched despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on four datasets, including backbone comparisons, hierarchical-consistency measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds tieredImageNet-H ViT results and a level-weight distribution ablation.

M1.justification: The orthogonal-subspace construction, transformation module, weighted KL loss, sparsity regularizer, and projection-based inference remain unchanged. The new HAVS definition and proofs formalize the existing method without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FGVC-Aircraft, CIFAR-100, iNaturalist-19, and tieredImageNet-H using the same classification tasks and hierarchies. The added ViT experiment changes the backbone configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Flamingo-I/II and HAFeat-I/II to the FGVC-Aircraft hierarchy-metric comparison. These methods already appeared in v1's hierarchical-consistency comparison in Table 4, so this is a local comparator expansion rather than four entirely new baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a frozen ViT-B16 configuration for tieredImageNet-H and controlled comparisons of decreasing, uniform, and increasing level weights. Existing dataset splits, evaluation metrics, and previously reported training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Table 8 tests whether concentrating projection weights toward coarse classes, distributing them uniformly, or emphasizing leaf classes affects classification. The earlier regularization, subspace-dimensionality, alpha-sensitivity, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both experimental-setup sections specify five seeds and means with 95% confidence intervals from a t-distribution with four degrees of freedom. Added result rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing matched result rows retain their values. v2 adds FGVC-Aircraft comparison metrics, tieredImageNet-H ViT results with cross-entropy/Hier-COS accuracy of 75.10%/74.71% and HOPS of 0.62/0.92, and weight-ablation accuracies of 51.08%, 70.22%, and 77.79% for decreasing, uniform, and increasing weights.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a formal HAVS definition, a theorem under explicit subspace-membership and nonzero-component assumptions, a parent-child subspace lemma, and a hierarchical-consistency proposition with appendix proofs. It also adds geometric claims involving Grassmannian distance. These substantially extend v1's mathematical treatment; the HOPS mathematics is largely relocated unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 makes HAVS and theoretical consistency central contributions and asserts that Hier-COS is the first unified hierarchy-aware/multilevel framework with adaptive capacity absent from existing methods. v1 already discussed multilevel prediction and adaptive dimensionality, but did not make these broad exclusivity claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a numerical-stability explanation for the weight function and interprets the new ablation as evidence supporting leaf-emphasized weights. It removes v1's span-versus-union discussion explaining why ideal subspace membership may fail in practice. The tieredImageNet-H accuracy-loss hypothesis and DAG/kernel-extension discussions largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the added ViT-B16 backbone and explains how reversed and uniform ablation weights are constructed. It drops the specific analysis-notebook and output-directory instructions, retaining a generic code-upon-acceptance statement. This changes documented access guidance without establishing actual resource availability.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from explicitly connecting Hier-COS to Long et al.'s subspace approach and Zhou et al.'s orthogonal transfer to stronger first-unified-framework and unique adaptive-capacity assertions. Those antecedent citations disappear, while discussion and citations concerning label-embedding trees, hierarchical detection, hyperbolic embeddings, and consistency-aware learning are added.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, related-work discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The method narrative is reorganized around HAVS, detailed HOPS construction moves to the appendix, and the supplement is restructured around proofs and geometric properties.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 6 gain rows, and a weight-ablation table is added. v1's conceptual Figure 8 and notation table are removed; Figure 6 is compressed from a full-width display to one column. Most existing graphics and table structures are retained, with revised placement and captions.

improvement.justification: The new weight ablation directly supports a previously untested design choice, and the added ViT comparison strengthens the experimental evidence. Formal definitions and conditional proofs also clarify the construction. These gains are limited by consistency claims broader than the proof's ideal-feature setting and by removal of explanatory displays and specific notebook access guidance.
